usage_requirements: Task prefixes are REQUIRED on every input: 'search_query: ' for queries, 'search_document: ' for corpus documents, 'clustering: ' for clustering, 'classification: ' for classification. Omitting them silently degrades retrieval quality.
L2-normalize embeddings (p=2, dim=1) for similarity use.

Matryoshka dimensionality reduction (512/256/128/64): in the raw-transformers path, apply layer normalization to the 768-d embedding BEFORE truncating to the target dim, then L2-normalize; in sentence-transformers use truncate_dim which handles this.
trust_remote_code=True required on transformers < v5.5.0 / sentence-transformers < v5.3.0 (custom NomicBert modeling code); newer versions load natively per the model card.
Custom modeling code depends on einops (when loaded via trust_remote_code).

Model was trained at 2048-token context; to use sequence lengths beyond 2048 (up to 8192) you must enable dynamic rotary scaling, e.g. rope_parameters={'rope_theta': 1000.0, 'rope_type': 'dynamic', 'factor': 2.0} (older snippets: rotary_scaling_factor=2).
known_issues: Repo references configuration/modeling files hosted in a separate repo (nomic-ai/nomic-bert-2048); offline/air-gapped or serialized copies (e.g. mlflow save of the sentence-transformers model) can fail because those files are re-downloaded at load time (HF discussions #12, #25).
Community has requested upstreaming the modeling code to avoid trust_remote_code and the einops dependency (HF discussion #16); resolved only on recent transformers/sentence-transformers versions.
Loading with safetensors: model ships as model.safetensors; older loading paths expecting pytorch_model.bin need safe_serialization handling (HF discussion #2).
Prefix handling is caller responsibility in most frameworks; serving layers (e.g. vLLM, kserve, privateGPT) have had trust_remote_code plumbing issues (see linked GitHub issues).
